core_obligations: Record that the forward implication is formal (proof line 2486).

For the converse, let k''/k be finite purely inseparable with a point x'' above x, and choose a common finitely generated extension k''' of k' and k'' together with a point of X_{k'''} above both x' and x'' (proof lines 2487-2492).

Apply descent of regularity along the flat local homomorphism between the local rings over k'' and over k''': the target is regular by hypothesis upstairs, so the source is regular, and the pointwise criterion then gives geometric regularity of X at x over k (proof lines 2493-2503).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to finite purely inseparable extensions and pick a common extension (proof lines 2487-2492).
Descend regularity along the flat local map (proof lines 2493-2503).
difficulty_reason: For X over k, a finitely generated extension k'/k, a point x of X and a point x' of X_{k'} above it, the lemma shows that geometric regularity at x is equivalent to geometric regularity at x' over k', with the global statement as a corollary (statement lines 2470-2483). The forward implication is formal. For the converse the author reduces to the defining condition on finite purely inseparable extensions: given such an extension k'' and a point x'' above x, one chooses a common finitely generated extension of k' and k'' and a point of the triple base change above both, and observes that the map between the two local rings is a flat local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings, hence faithfully flat; regularity upstairs therefore descends to the local ring over k'', and the pointwise criterion then gives geometric regularity over k (proof lines 2485-2503). The claim is H2: the reduction to finite purely inseparable extensions plus the faithfully flat descent of regularity, with the common extension field as the only auxiliary construction.
